Own-terms question: 'for the duration of the war and six months thereafter' could end the clause earlier than May 1, 1947 only if the war is treated as having ended before November 1, 1946. The held corpus gives only a recital (in EO 9857A) that hostilities ceased as proclaimed by Proclamation 2714 of December 31, 1946; six months after that is after May 1, 1947. The proclamation itself is not held, and the legal date of the war's end for this clause is not stated in any held source.

Section 2 applies only 'during the period the Civil Service Commission is operating under the War Service Regulations prescribed pursuant to Executive Order No. 9063'. EO 9691 section 9 (February 4, 1946, held) revokes EO 9063, and section 3 of EO 9691 requires normal Civil Service Rules actions within thirty days. When the Commission stopped operating under the War Service Regulations (February 4, 1946, about March 6, 1946, or later) is not stated in any held source; a Civil Service Commission regulation or notice is the missing source.
The machine inventory omits the lead of section 1 (the authorization itself, before paragraph (a)); a corrected inventory is needed.
EO 9691 section 8 re-grants the section 1 authority in broader terms on February 4, 1946 without revoking EO 9644; whether that supersedes section 1 is a further legal judgment.

The machine inventory repeats paragraph numbers (1, 4, 8 and their duplicates) across Subdivisions; each row would need to be tied to its Subdivision and checked against any amendment by EO 9830 Part II before submission.

The inventory has 16 rows (including repeated sub-paragraph letters and numbers) and the order carries several own-terms limits that may end individual clauses before May 1, 1947: section 3 (regulations for the transitional period 'until such time as the Civil Service Rules are revised' and all actions under the Rules within thirty days), the July 1, 1946 report to the President, section 4 (temporary appointments 'pending the establishment of appropriate registers'), section 5 and section 7 (the December 31, 1946 limit, replaced by EO 9815 on December 23, 1946). A clause-by-clause first-end decision, including which of these are conditions that ended before May 1, 1947, is not supportable from the held texts without a Civil Service Commission source on when registers were established and the Rules revised.
EO 9691 section 9 itself revokes EO 9063, EO 9378 and EO 8514 on signing; those are completed acts and do not bear on its own end.

No citable end source is registered in EO 9815's dossier (the view lists no ACT evidence at all). The end would be the revocation of EO 9691 by EO 9830 Part III (row 'No. 9691 of February 4, 1946.' at character 91965 of jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9830.txt, enacting clause 'effective May 1, 1947:' at character 2198), which needs a source-excerpt declaration the producer may not run.

Whether an amendment of a section ends with the revoked parent on the parent's end date, or when the 'general revision of Schedule A is promulgated' (EO 9830 was signed February 24, 1947, published February 25, effective May 1, 1947), is a legal judgment that the held text does not settle.

Rows ended earlier than EO 10480 and need row-by-row first-end decisions: EO 10377 section 2 (July 1952) revokes sections 403 to 410 of Part IV and inserts a new section 403; EO 10193 and EO 10200 (1950 and 1951) reassign functions; EO 10281 (August 28, 1951) amends and moves functions of sections 301 and 303; EO 10324 (February 6, 1952) amends section 901; EO 10433 (February 4, 1953) rewrites section 401(a); EO 10461 and Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1953 change the named agencies. The packet marks seven actor texts as 'target provision not located' (EO 10182, 10193, 10323, 10467 and others), so those chains lack citable evidence.
The 70-row inventory (including repeated sec403-b and sec601 duplicates) is too large to confirm in this pass; a sampled confirmation would not meet the completeness requirement.

EO 10461 section 5 abolishes the Office established by EO 10193 but section 6 makes the order effective only 'when the first Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization appointed under Reorganization Plan No. 3 of 1953 enters upon office'. That date is not in any held source (a Federal Register notice or appointment record is missing), so the first end between June 17 and August 14, 1953 cannot be fixed; EO 10480 section 607 supplies only an outer bound of August 14, 1953.

Earlier changes (EO 10200 and EO 10219 non-derogation sentences, EO 10433 section 2 amending section 401(a) of EO 10161 by reference to the Director) are later events needing row-by-row before-and-after text.

Clause-level ends differ: section 1 and its subparagraphs end with EO 10433 section 1(c) on February 4, 1953 (with boards and committees continued under the Director of Defense Mobilization 'unless and until other disposition thereof is made by him'), while sections 3 to 6 end at the latest with EO 10480; whether any of sections 3 to 6 ended with the Defense Production Administration (EO 10433) needs a clause-by-clause reading of the roughly 9,500-character section 1(c)(5) and the later amendments by EO 10219, EO 10223, EO 10281, EO 10301, EO 10324, EO 10359, EO 10373, EO 10377 and EO 10390, which the packet lists as chain events without located provisions ('target provision not located: EO:10193').

EO 10700 section 7 makes its provisions effective July 1, 1957 'except that if funds appropriated for the National Security Council shall not have become available on that date for the support of the Board', in which case on 'such later date as funds' become available. Whether funds were available on July 1, 1957 is not stated in any held source (an NSC appropriation record or EO 10700 implementation notice is missing), so the exact first-end date cannot be confirmed.

EO 10610 section 303(b) proviso and EO 10598 section 1 are amendments to be recorded as later events with before-and-after text; EO 10920 (February 1961, held APP) revokes EO 10700, not EO 10483, and is not an end of this order.
